metadata.title: THE ROLE OF SUBNATIONAL GOVERNMENTS IN ADULT SKILLS SYSTEMS: ITALY

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note is a governance and institutional mapping of Italy’s adult skills system, not an analysis of student microdata from an ILSA (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIAAC). As such, there is no sampling frame for students, no plausible-value (PV) scaling, and no complex survey design to weight. The document synthesizes information on responsibilities and stakeholders across national, regional, and local levels (ministries, agencies, regions, employment services, and providers) rather than estimating statistical relationships from assessment responses. Therefore, no student or replicate weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT, BRR/JRR) are applicable to the reported content.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because this document does not analyze cognitive assessment outcomes from an ILSA/PIAAC dataset at the student level. Instead, it provides a descriptive overview of governance structures, responsibilities, and expenditure allocation across levels of government. Missing-data handling is not reported because there is no statistical model estimation on incomplete respondent data; the note is based on institutional and policy information rather than survey responses.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Not applicable: the note does not use an ILSA/PIAAC student dataset or define an analytic sample; it describes governance arrangements for Italy’s adult skills system.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD country note describes how Italy’s adult skills system is governed across national, regional, and local levels, focusing on responsibilities for VET, CET, adult education (AE), Higher VET (HVET), and Active Labour Market Policies (ALMPs). It explains that strategic responsibilities are split between national ministries (Education and Merit; Labour and Social Policies; Universities and Research for HVET), while regional governments play the central role in designing and implementing policies, including funding and managing regional training and adult education centres. The note also details the roles of national agencies (e.g., evaluation and public policy analysis bodies), social partners, and regional observatories/councils that provide intelligence and coordination. Because the document is descriptive and does not estimate models from assessment data, there are no ML performance metrics, benchmarks, or PV-based achievement outcomes.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a non-empirical governance mapping note rather than an ILSA-based empirical study. Consequently, fields related to student sampling, PV handling, missing-data procedures, and ML model evaluation are structurally absent by design.
